topic: AI infrastructure demand, bottlenecks, and value capture
capture_method: curator-frozen extracts plus unadjusted market observations

extracts: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $30.0 billion, up 122% year over year.
Data Center revenue was $26.3 billion, up 154% year over year and 16% sequentially.
Management described strong Hopper demand and anticipation for Blackwell; forward statements still carry supply, execution, and customer-concentration risk.
Microsoft said the AI transition is both knowledge- and capital-intensive.
Roughly half of FY2024 and Q4 capital expense related to land, buildings, and finance leases, which management described as flexible assets monetized over 15 years or longer.
The same infrastructure serves platform, application, partner, and first-party SaaS demand, so capex cannot be attributed only to one AI product.
Vertiv reported 60% organic order growth in Q1 2024.
Management said the data-center market was accelerating with high-performance compute and that opportunity-pipeline velocity had increased.
The company sells power and thermal-management infrastructure, but orders, capacity conversion, margins, and valuation remain separate questions.
